answer: Every agent registers a TPM-sealed key plus a 300-token anchor bond. The registry hashes the chip's endorsement certificate, so one piece of silicon holds exactly one identity; a second enrollment from the same certificate is refused. When a peer challenges a newcomer, the key echoes back a fresh sealed quote that gets checked against the public chip database before any task is graded. A clone cluster spreads a lotus-shaped burn graph, slashing every linked bond inside 48 hours. Registering 10,000 fakes therefore needs 10,000 real chips, 3M tokens of bonds, and a month of smuggling.
